column1: # PROCESSED SYNTHETIC DATASET -- what each technique does and does not tell us
# DEMONSTRATION DATASET. Synthetically generated for portfolio purposes. These values were not measured on any instrument and do not describe a real sample.

column3: Crystal structure, phase identity, lattice parameter, crystallite size, microstrain
column4: d-spacings; a = lattice parameter (A); D_Scherrer (nm); microstrain eps
column5: Volume-weighted and blind to amorphous or poorly-ordered material; cannot separate Fe3O4 from gamma-Fe2O3 on peak position alone; Scherrer size is a coherent-domain size, NOT a particle size

column2: Vibrational modes -- local bonding and surface chemistry
column3: Fe-O lattice modes; adsorbed water; surface hydroxyls; presence/absence of organics
column4: Band positions (cm-1); relative intensities; band areas (semi-quantitative at best)
column5: Heavily overlapped bands in the Fe-O region; absorptivities are unknown so intensities are not concentrations; sampling geometry (ATR vs KBr) shifts band positions and intensities

column3: Charge-transfer absorption; qualitative optical behaviour; dispersion stability
column4: Absorbance vs wavelength; apparent Tauc intercepts (unreliable for this material)
column5: For a dispersion, measured absorbance mixes true absorption with Mie/Rayleigh turbidity; Fe3O4 is not a wide-gap semiconductor, so a Tauc 'band gap' is not a meaningful intrinsic property

column3: Particle/aggregate size, shape, degree of agglomeration, surface texture
column4: Size distribution statistics: mean, median, SD, quartiles, D[4,3], D[3,2]
column5: Measures whole features, so aggregates are counted as particles; thresholding choices shift the mean by several percent; limited field of view creates sampling bias; conductive coating inflates diameters

column3: Volatile content: adsorbed water, surface hydroxyls, organics (if present); thermal stability
column4: Mass loss per region (%); DTG peak temperatures (C); total volatile content (%)
column5: Gives mass change only, never chemical identity; results depend strongly on atmosphere, heating rate, sample mass and packing; in air, Fe3O4 oxidation causes a mass GAIN that can mask losses
